That is ~40 lines, not 879. Pattern A's failure is silent because the `except Exception: pass` swallows the `ModuleNotFoundError`, but the bug above (blocker) makes the crash surface at the outer `_install_fake_client()` call. Even after fixing the import name, the multiple-pattern patch is over-engineered: only one of these three locations is what `regintel/pipeline.run_all` actually resolves `get_async_client` from. Per `regintel/pipeline.py:17` the pipeline does `from dial.client import get_async_client`, so the single correct patch is `dial.client.get_async_client`. Evidence: `regintel/pipeline.py:17` shows the actual import.
issues.suggestedFix: After fixing the module name, simplify to a single patch site: `import dial.client; dial.client.get_async_client = lambda model=None: fake`. That is the location the real pipeline resolves the symbol from (verified by `from dial.client import get_async_client` in `regintel/pipeline.py:17`). Remove Patterns A and B.

issues.description: `FakeClassificationClient.classify` is defined as `async` but the real DIAL client interface (`AsyncOpenAI`) uses `chat.completions.create(...)`, not a top-level `classify(prompt)` coroutine. The pipeline does `client = get_async_client(model=model)` (regintel/pipeline.py:155) and passes it to `classify_event(event, client=client, ...)` which calls `client.chat.completions.create(...)` (regintel/classifier.py). Patching `get_async_client` to return a fake that has only a `classify(prompt)` method will cause `AttributeError` at the first model call. Evidence: `regintel/classifier.py` exposes `async def classify_event` which uses `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) make the fake implement the real `AsyncOpenAI.chat.completions.create` interface and return a fake `ChatCompletion` object whose `choices[0].message.content` is the JSON the scripted answer would have produced, or (b) replace the fake-client mechanism entirely with `monkeypatch.setattr('regintel.classifier.classify_event', AsyncMock(side_effect=...))`. Option (a) is the more faithful REGI-010-A implementation; option (b) is fewer lines.

issues.description: Append-only integrity violated: _backfill_duplicate_links() executes `UPDATE classifications SET duplicate_of = ? WHERE event_id = ? AND duplicate_of IS NULL` (scripts/run_pipeline.py:478-481). Review criterion 8 states classifications rows are never updated, only appended, and any UPDATE against that table is a blocker; regintel/store.py:9-10 documents the same invariant ('Classifications and reviews are append-only: there are no UPDATE or DELETE statements'). The docstring's framing of this as 'metadata completion of a null column' does not exempt it — this is now the only UPDATE against classifications in the codeline, and it rewrites a persisted classification row after the fact. The root cause is that the duplicate link is resolved after the row is appended instead of before: regintel/pipeline.py already has the deterministic, append-only mechanism — _build_dedup_record (regintel/pipeline.py:117-148) builds a zero-token duplicate ClassificationRecord with duplicate_of set — but the dedup short-circuit is guarded behind `if only_unclassified:` (regintel/pipeline.py:225), so the script's legacy fixture path never runs it and the model (which cannot name event_ids) leaves duplicate_of null.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the link before the row is appended, not after: lift the `only_unclassified` guard around the dedup pass in regintel/pipeline.py so the legacy fixture path also runs find_duplicate before the model call (this also satisfies the REGI-003 rule that deterministic dedup runs before any model call, and saves the RU-006 model call entirely). The appended classification row then carries duplicate_of from the start, the evidence row simply reads it, and _backfill_duplicate_links, the UPDATE, and the new `import sqlite3` can all be deleted — a smaller change that keeps evidence == database without breaking append-only.

issues.description: The 'lenient envelope' branch (classifier.py:405-437) bypasses resolve() for any model output that is a JSON object with a real-number confidence, hand-rolling a second, divergent resolution path instead of calling the helper this very story creates. Live verification (scripted FakeClient through classify_event) shows the wired path violates the story's escalation contract: (a) '{"bucket":"relevant","confidence":1.5,"rationale":"hi"}' persists bucket='relevant', confidence=1.5 — the story says confidence outside [0,1] must route to needs-review; (b) '{"bucket":"relevant","confidence":0.9}' (missing rationale) persists bucket='relevant' with an EMPTY rationale — the story says missing rationale routes to needs-review with 'model output unparseable: <reason>'; (c) '{"bucket":"relevant","confidence":0.5,"rationale":"model says low"}' persists rationale 'model says low' with NO 'low confidence (<value> < <threshold>): ' prefix — AC3 requires that prefix; (d) an out-of-vocabulary bucket persists a plain needs-review without the mandated 'model output unparseable' rationale. This is both an AC12 violation ('classify_event calls resolve() on model output ... in every outcome branch' — the lenient branch never calls it) and a CONCISION & REUSE violation: the diff hand-rolls logic that regintel.escalation.resolve already provides, correctly. Note on my iteration-2 approval: I approved without running the wired path end-to-end; this live reproduction is the evidence that changed my assessment — the divergence is real and reproducible, not a re-litigation.

Source: regintel/classifier.py:405-437 read directly; the branch guards on `isinstance(parsed, dict) and _is_real_number(parsed.get("confidence"))` and never calls resolve() inside it.
issues.suggestedFix: Delete the lenient branch entirely.
